detail.body:
## Overview

Enable FP8 MMA in the SM90 FA4 full-attention kernel ([PR199](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/199)) for Gemma-4 while retaining FP8 KV-cache storage.

Gemma-4 uses head dimension 512 for full attention and 256 for sliding-window attention. This change compares FP8 MMA against the existing path that reads FP8 KV, dequantizes it, and performs FP16 MMA.

On H200, FP8 full attention uses FA4, while FP8 sliding-window attention continues to use FA3. FA4 FP8 sliding-window attention with head dimension 256 is currently unsupported.

## Claims

- Integrate the SM90 d512 FP8-MMA kernel while preserving native FP16/BF16 queries and supported FA3 sliding-window routing.
- Gate unsupported kernel combinations and normalize descale layouts.
- Allow FA4 full-attention layers to select splits automatically, removing the previous CUDA-graph cap of 32 for these layers; retain the cap for FA3.
- Report measured gains over the KV-dequantization baseline and the remaining regression against BF16 KV/MMA.

## Validation
The MMA labels describe the **full-attention path**. Both FP8-KV configurations use FA3 FP8 sliding-window attention; the BF16-KV reference uses FA4 BF16 sliding-window attention.

Serving setup:

- Gemma-4-31B-it-FP8 weights for all configurations.
- Four H200 GPUs on one node; TP4.
- Approximately 25K shared prefix plus 3K unique input tokens.
- 128 requests, 200 output tokens per request.
- MTP enabled with three speculative tokens.
- Prefix-cache reuse enabled.
- Concurrency 1–64; median of three rounds.

### Serving performance
The `8k-in-1k-out` benchmark of [`gemma_4_31b_it_h200`](https://github.com/vllm-project/perf-eval/blob/main/workloads/gemma_4_31b_it_h200.yaml) on one H200 at TP=1, with GPU clocks locked. Each number is the median of 3 repetitions, as perf-eval aggregates them; no request failed.

| | Output tok/s | Mean TPOT (ms) | Median ITL (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before (`5d35ce3934` + FA `b273a02`) | 796.5 | 126.5 | 75.1 |
| This PR + vllm-project/flash-attention#199 | **831.1 (1.04x)** | **123.2** | **69.3** |
| Delta | +4.3% | -2.6% | -7.8% |

<details><summary>Reproduce</summary>

- Before is this PR's base, `5d35ce3934`, with FlashAttention at vllm-project/flash-attention#199's base, `b273a02`. After is this PR's head, `237043eee6`, with #199's head, `2648f1b`.
- Neither PR changes C++. Both runs use one editable build of `237043eee6` with `VLLM_FLASH_ATTN_SRC_DIR` set to the FlashAttention checkout, and differ only in Python sources.
- The model is a local copy of `RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-dynamic`. Server and benchmark match perf-eval@5f4e445 (`lib/server.sh`, `lib/run_vllm_bench.sh`, `lib/aggregate_perf.py`).

```bash
VLLM_DEEP_GEMM_WARMUP=skip VLLM_ENGINE_READY_TIMEOUT_S=3600 \
vllm serve $MODEL --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --tool-call-parser gemma4 --reasoning-parser gemma4 --enable-auto-tool-choice

# 3 repetitions against the same server; median of each metric
vllm bench serve --backend openai --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000 --model $MODEL \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 --ignore-eos \
  --num-prompts 512 --max-concurrency 128 --num-warmups 128
```

</details>

### Model evaluation
Accuracy scores are percentages. **87.19% for AIME 2025, 85.73% for GPQA Diamond (avg@16), and 86.86% for MMLU-Pro are measured in this PR; the two reference columns are reported baselines from [PR #48666](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48666).**

| Benchmark | FP8 KV + FP8 MMA ([PR199](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/199)) | FP8 KV + FP16 MMA (reference FA4) | 	BF16 TRITON |
|---|---|---|---|
| AIME 2025 (avg@64) | 87.19 | 86.88 | 87.29 |
| GPQA Diamond (avg@16) | 85.73* | 86.55 | 85.42 |
| MMLU-Pro | 86.86  | 86.64 | 86.44 |

\* Note that in a paird GPQA Diamond comparison using the same 198 questions and 16 seeds, FP8 MMA scored 85.73% versus 85.32% for the FP8 KV + FP16 MMA. The difference was +0.41 percentage points, with a paired question-bootstrap 95% interval of [−0.51, +1.36] points. Both runs had zero invalid or truncated answers. The table’s 86.55% reference is imported from PR [#48666](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48666) and is separate from this matched control.

### MTP speculative decoding

Mean acceptance length (**AL**), median of three rounds, from the same sweep as the serving-performance table above. All configurations use FP8 model weights, TP4 on four H200 GPUs, three speculative tokens, and prefix-cache reuse enabled. Each measurement completed **128/128 requests without errors**. AL includes the bonus token emitted per speculative step.

| Configuration | cc1 | cc2 | cc4 | cc8 | cc16 | cc32 | cc64 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| FP8 KV + FP8 MMA | 2.9830 | 2.9932 | 3.0002 | 2.9640 | 2.9849 | 2.9860 | 2.9793 |
| FP8 KV + FP16 MMA | 2.9924 | 2.9691 | 3.0130 | 2.9995 | 2.9993 | 2.9857 | 2.9979 |
| BF16 KV + BF16 MMA | 3.0053 | 2.9823 | 2.9940 | 2.9935 | 2.9995 | 3.0002 | 2.9982 |

## Reproduction commands
The Hopper FP8 MMA path supports text-only workloads. The commands use --hf-overrides '{"text_config":{"use_bidirectional_attention":null}}' to disable Gemma-4’s bidirectional/mm-prefix attention. Multimodal Gemma-4 with FP8 KV uses Triton instead of this kernel. FP8 sliding-window layers use FA3, so do not force FA4 globally.

Serve and benchmark: 25K shared prefix, TP4, MTP3, cache reuse on

* FP8 KV + FP8 MMA (this PR):

```bash
vllm serve "$MODEL" \
  --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --trust-remote-code --async-scheduling \
  --enable-prefix-caching --attention-backend FLASH_ATTN \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 256 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --compilation-config '{"use_inductor_graph_partition":1,"pass_config":{"eliminate_noops":true,"fuse_allreduce_rms":true}}' \
  --hf-overrides '{"text_config":{"use_bidirectional_attention":null}}' \
  --speculative-config "{\"model\":\"$ASSISTANT\",\"num_speculative_tokens\":3}"
```

* FP8 KV + FP16 MMA (PR [#164](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/164) baseline kernel environment):
(The two FP8-KV serving commands are identical because MMA selection depends on the FlashAttention kernel source, not a CLI flag. For the control, we kept the same vLLM integration but replaced its vendored CuTe sources with the PR [#164](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/164) dequantizing kernel, including the baseline safety fixes, then restarted the server. --kv-cache-dtype fp8 selects FP8 cache storage in both cases)

```bash
vllm serve "$MODEL" \
  --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --trust-remote-code --async-scheduling \
  --enable-prefix-caching --attention-backend FLASH_ATTN \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 256 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --compilation-config '{"use_inductor_graph_partition":1,"pass_config":{"eliminate_noops":true,"fuse_allreduce_rms":true}}' \
  --hf-overrides '{"text_config":{"use_bidirectional_attention":null}}' \
  --speculative-config "{\"model\":\"$ASSISTANT\",\"num_speculative_tokens\":3}"
```

* BF16 KV + BF16 MMA:

```bash
vllm serve "$MODEL" \
  --max-num-seqs 64 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-model-len 32768 \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --trust-remote-code --async-scheduling \
  --enable-prefix-caching --attention-backend FLASH_ATTN \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 256 --kv-cache-dtype bfloat16 \
  --compilation-config '{"use_inductor_graph_partition":1,"pass_config":{"eliminate_noops":true,"fuse_allreduce_rms":true}}' \
  --hf-overrides '{"text_config":{"use_bidirectional_attention":null}}' \
  --speculative-config "{\"model\":\"$ASSISTANT\",\"num_speculative_tokens\":3}"
```

These recorded runs left the FA version unset. The dequantized control uses the PR [#164](https://github.com/vllm-project/flash-attention/pull/164) baseline kernel environment.

Benchmark:

```bash
aiperf profile \
  --model "$MODEL" --tokenizer "$MODEL" --tokenizer-trust-remote-code \
  --endpoint-type chat --endpoint /v1/chat/completions --streaming \
  --use-legacy-max-tokens --url http://127.0.0.1:8000 \
  --input-file "$DATASET" \
  --extra-inputs max_tokens:200 --extra-inputs min_tokens:200 \
  --extra-inputs ignore_eos:true --extra-inputs skip_special_tokens:false \
  --random-seed 1234 --use-server-token-count \
  --concurrency 16 --request-count 128 --num-dataset-entries 128
```

Run at concurrency 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, and 64; report the median of three rounds.

<details>
<summary>Evaluation commands</summary>

Evaluation server on four H200 GPUs. AIME and GPQA use `--max-num-seqs 16`; MMLU-Pro uses `32`. No MTP.

```bash
vllm serve "$MODEL" --served-model-name gemma \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 1 --data-parallel-size 4 \
  --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill --max-num-seqs 16 \
  --kv-cache-memory-bytes 101716968203 --enforce-eager \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 \
  --attention-backend FLASH_ATTN \
  --attention-config.flash_attn_version=3 --block-size 64 \
  --kernel-config.enable_flashinfer_autotune=false \
  --kernel-config.enable_cutedsl_warmup=false \
  --hf-overrides '{"text_config":{"use_bidirectional_attention":null}}'
```

**AIME 2025, avg@64**

Use `aime.yaml` with 64 samples per problem, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, and the GPT-4.1 judge configuration. Export `INFERENCE_API_KEY`.

```bash
docker run --rm --network host --shm-size=100g \
  -e DUMMY_API_KEY=dummy -e INFERENCE_API_KEY \
  -v "$PWD/aime.yaml:/config.yaml:ro" \
  -v "$PWD/aime-results:/results" \
  --entrypoint bash nvcr.io/nvidia/eval-factory/simple-evals:26.03 \
  -lc 'runner=$(command -v nemo-evaluator || command -v eval-factory); exec "$runner" run_eval --run_config /config.yaml'
```

**GPQA Diamond, avg@16**

Use `gpqa.yaml` with all 198 questions, the `eval/aai/mcq-4choices` prompt, temperature 1.0, and top-p 0.95. Run seeds 0–15.

```bash
pids=()
for seed in $(seq 0 15); do
  docker run --rm --network host --shm-size=4g \
    -e DUMMY_API_KEY=dummy -e HF_TOKEN \
    -e NEMO_EVALUATOR_TELEMETRY_LEVEL=0 -e OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \
    -v "$PWD/gpqa.yaml:/config.yaml:ro" \
    -v "$PWD/gpqa-results/seed-$seed:/results" \
    --entrypoint bash "$EVAL_IMAGE" \
    -lc 'runner=$(command -v nemo-evaluator || command -v eval-factory); exec "$runner" run_eval --run_config /config.yaml "$@"' \
    -- --overrides "config.params.extra.args=++prompt_config=eval/aai/mcq-4choices ++inference.random_seed=$seed" &
  pids+=("$!")
done

status=0
for pid in "${pids[@]}"; do
  wait "$pid" || status=1
done
test "$status" -eq 0
```

**MMLU-Pro**

Restart the evaluation server with `--max-num-seqs 32`. Use `mmlu.yaml` with all 12,032 questions, one sample per question, the `eval/aai/mcq-10choices-boxed` prompt, temperature 1.0, and top-p 0.95.

```bash
mkdir -p mmlu-results
chmod 777 mmlu-results

docker run --rm --network host --shm-size=4g \
  -e DUMMY_API_KEY=dummy -e HF_TOKEN \
  -e NEMO_EVALUATOR_TELEMETRY_LEVEL=0 -e OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 \
  -v "$PWD/mmlu.yaml:/config.yaml:ro" \
  -v "$PWD/mmlu-results:/results" \
  --entrypoint bash "$EVAL_IMAGE" \
  -lc 'runner=$(command -v nemo-evaluator || command -v eval-factory); exec "$runner" run_eval --run_config /config.yaml'
```

</details>

## Details

### Why FP8 is slower than BF16

Nsight shows that faster FP8 full attention does not necessarily produce faster end-to-end execution.

#### Sliding-window attention and KV-cache operations offset full-attention gains

The profiling setup uses 25K inputs, TP4, MTP enabled, prefix reuse enabled, and offered concurrency 64.

| Target-model kernel work | FP8 KV + FP8 MMA | BF16 KV + BF16 MMA | FP8 time reduction vs. BF16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Full attention | **6.681 ms** | 7.584 ms | **+11.9%** |
| Sliding-window attention | 5.482 ms | **4.206 ms** | −30.3% |
| KV-cache writes | 0.261 ms | **0.157 ms** | −66.2% |
| Attention preparation | 0.105 ms | 0 | N/A |
| Whole-cycle GPU span | 29.879 ms | **29.391 ms** | −1.7% |

Time reduction is `100 × (BF16 time − FP8 time) / BF16 time`, calculated from the displayed times. Positive values mean less time (faster); negative values mean more time (slower). 

Full attention is approximately **12% faster**, but sliding-window attention is approximately **30% slower**, with additional KV-write, preparation, and combine work.

KV-write overhead refers to the kernels that reshape and write newly generated keys and values into the paged cache, including the FP8 conversion/quantization path. Attention reads and prefix-cache reuse accounting are separate from this kernel category.

Reuse-off profiles show the same pattern.
The following comparison uses **cc16**, 25K inputs, TP4, MTP enabled, and prefix-cache reuse disabled. These matched pure-decode cycles process **16 active requests per target step**. Values are medians across four GPU ranks of each rank's per-cycle medians, with 69 matched cycles per rank for BF16 and 87 for FP8.

| Target-model kernel work | FP8 KV + FP8 MMA | BF16 KV + BF16 MMA | FP8 time reduction vs. BF16 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Full attention | **1.9670 ms** | 2.4358 ms | **+19.2%** |
| Sliding-window attention | 1.9593 ms | **1.3867 ms** | −41.3% |
| KV-cache writes | 0.2551 ms | **0.1413 ms** | −80.5% |
| Attention preparation | 0.1098 ms | 0 | N/A |
| Whole-cycle GPU span | 14.6594 ms | **14.2903 ms** | −2.6% |

Full attention is faster, but SWA, KV-cache writes, and attention preparation/combine offset the gain. The whole-cycle GPU span is **2.6% longer** for FP8. This is a profiling comparison, not an unprofiled end-to-end throughput measurement.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Routing of the FA4 SM90 FP8 MMA path (head_size=512 with an FP8 KV cache).
+
+The device capability is mocked, so no GPU is needed.
+"""
+
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.platforms.interface import DeviceCapability
+
+fa_interface = pytest.importorskip(
+    "vllm.vllm_flash_attn.flash_attn_interface",
+    reason="requires compiled CUDA flash-attention extensions",
+    exc_type=ImportError,
+)
+
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.fa_utils import get_flash_attn_version  # noqa: E402
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.flash_attn import (  # noqa: E402
+    FlashAttentionBackend,
+    FlashAttentionImpl,
+)
+
+SM80 = DeviceCapability(8, 0)
+SM90 = DeviceCapability(9, 0)
+SM100 = DeviceCapability(10, 0)
+
+
+@contextmanager
+def _device(capability, *, head_size, kv_cache_dtype, fa_version=None, dcp=1):
+    platform = MagicMock()
+    platform.is_xpu.return_value = False
+    platform.is_rocm.return_value = False
+    platform.is_cuda.return_value = True
+    platform.get_device_capability.return_value = capability
+    platform.is_device_capability_family.side_effect = (
+        lambda family, device_id=0: capability.to_int() // 10 == family // 10
+    )
+    config = MagicMock()
+    config.attention_config.flash_attn_version = fa_version
+    config.model_config.is_diffusion = False
+    config.model_config.get_head_size.return_value = head_size
+    config.cache_config.cache_dtype = kv_cache_dtype
+    config.parallel_config.decode_context_parallel_size = dcp
+    config.parallel_config.dcp_comm_backend = "ag_rs"
+    backends = "vllm.v1.attention.backends"
+    with (
+        patch(f"{backends}.fa_utils.current_platform", platform),
+        patch(f"{backends}.flash_attn.current_platform", platform),
+        patch.object(fa_interface, "is_fa_version_supported", return_value=True),
+        patch("vllm.config.get_current_vllm_config_or_none", return_value=config),
+        patch(
+            f"{backends}.flash_attn.get_current_vllm_config_or_none",
+            return_value=config,
+        ),
+        patch(
+            "vllm.distributed.parallel_state.get_dcp_world_size_and_rank",
+            return_value=(dcp, 0),
+        ),
+    ):
+        yield
+
+
+def _supports_combination(capability, head_size, kv_cache_dtype, block_size=64):
+    return FlashAttentionBackend.supports_combination(
+        head_size=head_size,
+        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        kv_cache_dtype=kv_cache_dtype,
+        block_size=block_size,
+        use_mla=False,
+        has_sink=False,
+        use_sparse=False,
+        use_mm_prefix=False,
+        device_capability=capability,
+    )
+
+
+def _impl(head_size, kv_cache_dtype):
+    return FlashAttentionImpl(
+        num_heads=8,
+        head_size=head_size,
+        scale=head_size**-0.5,
+        num_kv_heads=1,
+        alibi_slopes=None,
+        sliding_window=None,
+        kv_cache_dtype=kv_cache_dtype,
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "head_size,kv_cache_dtype,fa_version,sm90_fp8_mma",
+    [
+        (512, "fp8", 4, True),
+        (512, "fp8_e4m3", 4, True),
+        # Gemma-4 sliding-window layers stay on FA3 FP8 with an FP8 query.
+        (256, "fp8", 3, False),
+        (512, "auto", 4, False),
+    ],
+)
+def test_sm90_routing(head_size, kv_cache_dtype, fa_version, sm90_fp8_mma):
+    with _device(SM90, head_size=head_size, kv_cache_dtype=kv_cache_dtype):
+        assert get_flash_attn_version(head_size=head_size) == fa_version
+        assert _supports_combination(SM90, head_size, kv_cache_dtype) is None
+        impl = _impl(head_size, kv_cache_dtype)
+    assert impl.vllm_flash_attn_version == fa_version
+    # The FP8 MMA kernel quantizes Q in-kernel, so vLLM must not quantize it.
+    assert impl.supports_quant_query_input is not sm90_fp8_mma
+
+
+def test_sm90_fp8_mma_block_size():
+    with _device(SM90, head_size=512, kv_cache_dtype="fp8"):
+        assert FlashAttentionBackend.get_supported_kernel_block_sizes() == [64]
+        assert "block size" in _supports_combination(SM90, 512, "fp8", 16)
+    with _device(SM90, head_size=512, kv_cache_dtype="auto"):
+        assert _supports_combination(SM90, 512, "auto", 16) is None
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "capability,head_size,fa_version",

Thanks @katec846, this is a nice, compact integration. Overall the vLLM wiring looks good to me.

**Before merge:** `GIT_TAG` in `cmake/external_projects/vllm_flash_attn.cmake` points at 6d71c3f9, the head of FA PR 199. That commit is only reachable as `refs/pull/199/head` in vllm-project/flash-attention, so source builds without `VLLM_FLASH_ATTN_SRC_DIR` can't fetch it. So this should wait until FA PR 199 is merged and the tag is re-pinned to the merged commit on main (a squash merge gives a new SHA).

### Fixes you can cherry-pick

I put a few small fixes on a branch on top of your head (5446e6ce): https://github.com/simon-veitner-redhat/vllm/tree/pr60372-review-fixes

[`5b06e28`](https://github.com/simon-veitner-redhat/vllm/commit/5b06e28bfe70a1bdf99e871d535f2a781c8be32e) Remove the FA4 -> FA3 FP8 fallback in `flash_attn_varlen_func`, because no in-tree caller can reach it. Every caller that can pass `fa_version=4` with an FP8 K on SM90 is gated earlier to q/k/v head_size 512 with BF16/FP16 Q, so it always takes the FP8 MMA path. The main gates are the FP8 KV check in `FlashAttentionImpl.__init__` and the DiffKV init check, plus `supports_quant_query_input=False` on this path. The wrapper now raises a `NotImplementedError` that names the q/k/v dtypes and head sizes. The commit message lists every caller with file:line evidence.
2. [`43475aa`](https://github.com/simon-veitner-redhat/vllm/commit/43475aae57c0a462497acc5fc93f726fcc5547e3) Reject DCP with FA4 SM90 FP8 KV at impl init. DCP context attention is non-causal, so today a DCP server starts and then crashes on the first prefill with cached context.
3. [`8cb6afa`](https://github.com/simon-veitner-redhat/vllm/commit/8cb6afa3978dbb6f328d89914e13c91c9426ca15) CPU selector test for the new routing: SM90 + FP8 + d512 goes to FA4 FP8 MMA, while d256, BF16 KV, non-SM90 and DCP get the expected fallback or error. It also checks that the wrapper raises for FA4 + FP8 K below d512 without calling FA3. It runs in the existing V1 Attention step.
4. [`f52595b`](https://github.com/simon-veitner-redhat/vllm/commit/f52595b797b3722350dc83645ffc65785b48772d) GSM8K config for Gemma-4-31B-it-FP8 with `--kv-cache-dtype fp8` (TP2, text-only override) plus a 2x H100 lm-eval step, because nothing in CI covers this path yet. It measured 0.970 on 2x H200, and the threshold is 0.96.

### PR description

Could you update the description with the following?

- **Exact commands** for serve, bench and evals, including `--hf-overrides '{"text_config":{"use_bidirectional_attention":null}}'`. Without it the FP8 MMA kernel doesn't run.
- **The text-only limitation.** Gemma-4 is an mm-prefix LM by default, and on Hopper FLASH_ATTN with FP8 KV rejects mm-prefix, so multimodal Gemma-4 with FP8 KV uses Triton, not this kernel.
- **Numbers that disagree:**
  - The text says AIME 2025 is 85.78, but the table shows 87.19.
  - The stated ranges don't match the table. The table gives +0.2% to +2.6% over the dequant control (text: 0.5-2.2%) and -2.1% to -6.9% against BF16 (text: 3.7-9.8%).
  - GPQA is 1.39 points below the dequant reference (85.16 vs 86.55). A stderr or a rerun would help, and so would saying where the GPQA and MMLU-Pro values for this PR come from.
  - The control is labeled "FP16 MMA" in one table and "BF16 MMA" in the others.
- **The `aot_schedule` change** (`flash_attn.py:717`) is a behavior change, not a "preserve". On main with FP8 KV, the FA4 d512 layers were capped at 32 splits under CUDA graphs. Now FA4 picks the split count, and `flash_attn_max_num_splits_for_cuda_graph` no longer applies to these layers. Most of the high-concurrency gain comes from this change (numbers below), so it should get the credit in the performance section.
- **The checklist boxes.** The commits are co-authored by Codex, but the "AI assistance was used" and `/pr-checklist` boxes are unchecked.

### Our independent results

All runs used 4x H200 with `RedHatAI/gemma-4-31B-it-FP8-dynamic` and the text-only override. We compared main (FA dequant kernel) against this PR (FA PR 199), and the FA4 path was confirmed with a call tracer.

- **GSM8K** (lm-eval, 5-shot, chat template, 1319 questions; stderr is about 0.5). With FP8 KV: 95.68 with this PR vs 96.44 on main. With BF16 KV: 96.13 on both. The repo's own gsm8k harness gives 0.970 on the branch above.
- **Single-needle NIAH** from 4k to 248k tokens: 70/70 for every config.
- **Throughput** (TP4, no MTP, output tok/s, this PR vs main with FP8 KV):

  | Workload | cc 1 | high cc |
  |---|---|---|
  | prefill 16k/64 | +1.0% | +0.9% (cc32) |
  | prefill 32k/64 | +1.8% | +1.2% (cc8) |
  | mixed 4k/512 | -0.4% | +5.7% (cc128) |
  | decode 1k/1k | -0.7% | +11.5% (cc128) |

  FP8 KV is still 1-10% slower than BF16 KV, in line with what you report.

  Most of the high-concurrency gain comes from removing the 32-split cap. We checked this end to end by running this PR's vLLM code with main's FA, which keeps the dequant kernel but drops the cap. On decode at cc32 / cc128 that gives +4.5% / +11.3% over main, which is 94-100% of the full PR's +4.4% / +12.0%. On mixed it gives +2.9% / +4.8%, which is 81-84% of the PR's +3.4% / +6.0%. The FP8 MMA kernel itself adds about 0-1%.
- **BF16 is unchanged:** BF16 KV decode is within ±0.2% of main at cc 1-128. Main already uses FA4 for all Gemma-4 layers with BF16 KV, so the split change doesn't touch that path.

One small observation, not a blocker: in a harder multi-value retrieval test (6 values plus 10 distractor keys) at 196k tokens, mean recall was slightly lower with this PR. It was 0.86 vs 0.94 on main, over 36 trials (p≈0.06). The results were identical up to 64k and similar at 254k. I'm mentioning it for awareness only.

Right that the new kernel can't serve DCP's non-causal context call: the SM90 FP8 MMA kernel from FA#199 only builds its split QK accumulation for causal and local masks. But no working setup is lost, because DCP never worked on this path in vLLM, before or after this PR.

The FP8 MMA path only applies to head-size-512 layers with an FP8 KV cache on SM90, which means Gemma-4. On main (merge-base `5d35ce3`, FA pin `b273a02`), DCP fails for every Gemma-4 before it reaches this kernel:
- vLLM rejects DCP for any model with sliding-window layers ("DCP not support sliding window." at `vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py:950`), and every Gemma-4 has them.
- 31B and 26B-A4B also need TP greater than their 16 and 8 KV heads.
- E2B/E4B KV-shared layers pass `key=None` into `_forward_with_dcp` and raise `TypeError`.
- FA3 sliding layers with an FP8 KV cache crash under DCP with "query and key must have the same dtype".

The old fp16-dequant FA4 kernel computed the non-causal call correctly when called directly (rel L2 1.60e-3 on a captured Gemma-4 31B layer, H100), but no real config could reach it, and it no longer exists at `9ed6b12`.

This PR makes the limitation explicit: `FlashAttentionImpl.__init__` raises `NotImplementedError` for SM90 FA4 FP8 KV with `dcp_world_size > 1`, and the wrapper raises on non-causal FP8 MMA calls. With the guard bypassed the kernel runs but is less accurate (rel L2 2.62e-3, LSE error 0.062 vs 0.029 causal), so keeping the guard is right.

For reference, if DCP ever gains sliding-window support: running the context call as local attention with a window covering every key gives the same mask and uses the accurate local build. It matched the BF16-cache DCP path in a DCP=2 emulation on the same layer (rel L2 2.38e-3 vs 2.29e-3 decode). It's a workaround that relies on FA building the QK split for local masks; the cleaner fix would be in FA.
